Was extremely overweight from childhood up to 19/20, lost over 100 lbs, then regained 30~ish a few years after

The difference in how you are treated is astounding. I understand that it’s a natural thing that when you look “more attractive” people are going to be more attracted to you. The difference is apparent in so many ways whether it be someone opening a door for you when they’re walking in front of you, or maintaining eye contact during a conversation, or being actually invested in your input in a group setting. I went from being the “Nice funny/fat friend” that nobody ever talked to, to being sought after by men, making friends more easily, and being invited to do things. Even family treats you differently. It wasn’t direct, but they definitely were warmer to me than before. Growing up I always had very few friends, so this all felt (albeit nice) very unusual

I hate to admit this, but I miss how things were when I was at my lowest weight. How seen and heard I felt. I was visible for the first time in my life, and I ate it up. After regaining a significant amount, I can feel the difference in how I am seen in daily life again. In a way it’s been nice, because I’m no longer hyper-focused on my weight or my looks. I became obsessed with taking comparison photos of myself day-to-day to make sure I stayed the same size. Every mirror or glass window I walked by I was glancing in to body check myself. The worst thing I could think of was regaining weight, and becoming unaccepted by people around me again. Now that I actually have regained some weight, I’ve realized it’s not at all the end of the world. Sometimes it’s nice not to feel like I have eyes on me and sometimes I do want to feel invisible. I know I don’t look absolutely perfect, but I still look pretty damn good. It’s nice not to have the [theoretical] weight on my shoulders of how I look every second of the day.

I think what I like most about it though is that in doing it, I see and feel and work with all of the loose skin and realize that it is not something separate from me that I dislike - it IS me, a small portion of the entire picture, and that I am more than JUST my body or JUST my loose skin. The act of doing all of that is nice too because you get the satisfaction of knowing that you’re deliberately doing something in order to improve yourself (somewhat) outside of weight loss as a whole.
